subject: Finding model selection proportions for model averaging

messages.author: 06199470668a2843
messages.subject: Finding model selection proportions for model averaging
parts:
Dear list members,

I am currently using Distance 5.0 Rel 2 to analyse a largish farmland bir=
d
data set obtained through line transects. For some subsets it has turned
out that there exist several different models that would fit the data
about equally well. I am attempting to use model averaging by
bootstrapping to select among those - e.g., 3 different models and 1000
bootstrap runs. What I haven't been able to find out is how to extract
from the results of these runs some indication as to the proportion of
these 1000 runs that were fitted with model 1,2 or 3, respectively. The
bootstrap output file does not seem to contain the relevant information
(maybe I got a bit lost in the format though - according to the
documentation, module #2/statistic #13 would seem to contain what I want
to find out, but the file references no 2-digit statistics codes at all).

Having just read the Buckland et al., June 1997 Biometrics paper, where
this kind of information was fruitfully applied, I'd be grateful if
someone could give me a hint how to extract it from my data!

cheers
florian

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: Finding model selection proportions for model averaging
parts:
Hi Florian (list),

You can tell from current bootstrap stats file output which model was
selected for each run by looking at the 3rd column of numbers
(Estimator) for lines where the 4th column (Module) is 2. The number
in the Estimator column tells you which of the estimators you allowed
Distance to choose among was actually chosen. So, for example, if in
the Model Defintion Properties, Detection function | Estimate tab you
had selected
Half-normal Cosine
Uniform Cosine
Half-normal Hermite polynomial
then bootstrap replicates where the Estimator column has a 1 in it
correspond with the Half-normal/Cosine model, 2 corresponds to the
Uniform/Cosine model and 3 corresponds to the half-normal/Hermite model.
Hope this makes sense. Note this is only true when the 4th column
(Module) is 2 -- ie for rows that deal with detection function estimation.

You were looking for Module 2, statistic 13 (key function type). That
is present in the stats file (the one produced from the original, not
bootstrapped data), along with statistics 14-17 and 101+ (see manual for
details of these). However, you helped me locate a bug where these are
not produced in the bootstrap stats file. I have now fixed that bug, so
all of these statistics are now produced for each bootstrap replicate.
If you want an updated copy of the mcds analysis engine, mcds.exe then
email me off the list. The fix will be generally available in the next
release of Distance.

Cheers,

- Len
